t: What Parts Bins and Sorting Trays Are
title: What Parts Bins and Sorting Trays Are
description: Parts bins are open-front stackable containers (the Akro-Mils style) that hold larger loose components — fans, brackets, manuals, cable bags — visible and grabbable. Sorting trays are segmented flat trays for staging teardown parts. Bins are the bulk tier of organization: too big for the grid box, too small for the shelf, they live on the bench wall or cart in plain sight.

demo.program:
print("Bins: open-front, stackable, for BULK loose parts (fans, brackets, manuals).")
print("Sorting trays: segmented flat, for teardown staging.")
print("The bulk tier: too big for grid box, too small for shelf. Visible + grabbable.")

title: Akro-Mils Style Bins: The Standard
description: Akro-Mils bins are the industry standard — polypropylene, open hopper front, stackable, with label holders and optional dividers. Sizes run from small (5x4x3 in) for screws-by-the-handful to large (11x11x5 in) for fans and PSUs. They hang on louvered panels or stack on benches. Buy one size family so everything stacks and hangs together.

t: Bin Wall Systems: Louvered Panels and Rails
title: Bin Wall Systems: Louvered Panels and Rails

A 24x36-inch panel holds dozens of small bins: one bin per part type, labeled, at eye level. The wall system turns 'somewhere in a drawer' into 'third row, second bin'. Visibility is the feature: you see stock levels at a glance.

t: Labeling Bins: The System That Scales
title: Labeling Bins: The System That Scales
description: Every bin gets a label: part name, spec, and minimum stock (for the kanban bins). Label holders on the bin front take standard inserts — printed labels beat tape. Color-code by category: blue bins for fasteners, red for electrical, green for cooling. A labeled wall of bins is a pick-and-place system a stranger could use.

print("Color: blue fasteners, red electrical, green cooling.")
print("Labeled wall = pick-and-place a stranger could use.")

title: Bin Dividers and Sub-Compartments
description: Dividers split bins into sub-compartments — a fan bin divides into 120mm/140mm/200mm, a cable bin into SATA/power/extension. The divider keeps one bin doing the work of three without mixing. Adjustable dividers reconfigure per stock; fixed dividers suit stable inventory. Divided bins are where the organization compounds.

t: Bins vs Grid Boxes vs Drawers
title: Bins vs Grid Boxes vs Drawers
description: Bins: bulky parts, visible, grabbable — the bulk tier. Grid boxes: small parts, sorted, lidded — the precision tier. Drawers: hidden storage for stock and rarely-used — the archive tier. The three tiers handle every part size: bins for hands, boxes for fingers, drawers for storage. Missing a tier means parts in the wrong place.

demo.program:
print("bins   : bulky, visible, grabbable. HANDS tier.")
print("grid box: small, sorted, lidded. FINGERS tier.")
print("drawers : hidden stock, rarely-used. ARCHIVE tier.")
print("Every part size has a tier: missing one = parts in wrong places.")

title: Buying Guide: Bins Worth Buying
description: Buy: sturdy polypropylene (not brittle thin plastic), one size family (stacking/hanging interoperates), label holders included, optional dividers available. A starter wall — panel plus 20 mixed bins — runs 60-100 dollars and transforms a shop. Avoid dollar-store bins: they crack, don't stack, and the 'savings' become a rebuy.

title: Kanban Restocking for Bin Walls
description: Each shop bin gets a kanban card with the part, supplier, and reorder point — when stock hits the card, the card goes to the buy board. The wall manages its own restocking: empty-ish bins signal visibly, cards carry the ordering info. No spreadsheets, no stockouts mid-job — the physical system does the inventory thinking.

title: Dust and Bin Maintenance
description: Open bins collect dust — the trade-off for visibility. Quarterly, dump and wipe bins, check labels, and audit stock against kanban minimums. In dusty shops, bin covers or a quick daily blowout keeps parts clean. The maintenance is the price of the visibility; the visibility is worth it.

print("Dusty shops: covers or daily blowout. Price of visibility; worth it.")
print("Open = dusty. Covered = hidden. Choose per shop, maintain the choice.")
